before: declare(strict_types=1); near the start of a PHP file makes scalar arguments at calls in that file strict. It is not a global switch for every file.
A strict int parameter does not accept "4" just because its text looks numeric. The call throws TypeError.
An int can be accepted for a float declaration under strict typing. Strict mode is not a promise that absolutely every accepted value has identical source type.
This lesson deliberately leaves the changed TypeError uncaught so the local process fails. Later lessons show catch blocks.
Expected output or behavior: 8. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

before.question: In this strict calling file, replace twice(4) with twice("4"). What happens?
choices: It prints 8 because strict mode only affects return values.
It prints 44 because strings repeat automatically.
It throws TypeError because the int parameter rejects this string.
before.explanation: The strict call requires an acceptable integer argument; numeric-looking text is not an integer.

after.question: In this strict file, what happens if four is passed as text?
after.explanation: The function requires an integer and the strict call supplied text.
